verses.sanskrit:
शकुनिरुवाच॥
              बहुवित्तं पराजैषीः पाण्डवानां युधिष्ठिर। आचक्ष्व वित्तं कौन्तेय यदि तेऽस्त्यपराजितम्॥१॥
verses.english: Shakuni said O Yudhisthira, you have lost much wealth of the Pandavas. O son of Kunti, if you have any other wealth which is not yet lost, tell us.

verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              मम वित्तमसङ्ख्येयं यदहं वेद सौबल। अथ त्वं शकुने कस्माद्वित्तं समनुपृच्छसि॥२॥
verses.english: Yudhisthira said O Shakuni, O son of Subala, I know my wealth is untold. Why do you ask me of my wealth?

verses.sanskrit: अयुतं प्रयुतं चैव शङ्कुं पद्मं तथार्बुदम्। खर्वं शङ्खं निखर्वं च महापद्मं च कोटयः॥३॥
verses.english: You can bet (with me) tens of thousands, and millions, tens of millions and billions, hundreds of billions and trillions, tens of trillions and hundreds of trillions, tens of quadrillions and hundreds of quadrillions and even more. O king, I will bet such wealth. With this wealth at stake I shall play with you.

verses.sanskrit: मध्यं चैव परार्धं च सपरं चात्र पण्यताम्। एतन्मम धनं राजंस्तेन दीव्याम्यहं त्वया॥४॥

वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एतच्छुत्वा व्यवसितो निकृतिं समुपाश्रितः। जितमित्येव शकुनिर्युधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥५॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Having heard this and adopting unfair means Shakuni, ever ready with the dice, said to Yudhishthira, "Lo, I have won?"

verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              गवाश्वं बहुधेनूकमसङ्ख्येयमजाविकम्। यत्किञ्चिदनुपर्णाशां प्राक्सिन्धोरपि सौबल। एतन्मम धनं सर्वं तेन दीव्याम्यहं त्वया॥६॥
verses.english: Yudhisthira said O son of Subala, I have innumerable kine, horses, milch cows with claves, goats and shee; in the country extending from the Parnasha to the eastern bank of the Sindhu (river). With this wealth I shall (now) play with you.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एतच्छुत्वा व्यवसितो निकृतिं समुपाश्रितः। जितमित्येव शकुनिर्युधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥७॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Having heard this and adopting unfair means, Shakuni, ever ready with the dice, sand to Yudhishthira, “Lo, I have won?"

verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              पुरं जनपदो भूमिरब्राह्मणधनैः सह। अब्राह्मणाश्च पुरुषा राजञ्च्छिष्टं धनं मम। एतद्राजन्मम धनं तेन दीव्याम्यहं त्वया॥८॥
verses.english: Yudhisthira said O king, I have my city, the country, land, the wealth of horses thereon, except those belonging to the Brahmanas, and also all those persons, except Brahmanas living therein-the wealth which still belongs to me. With all this wealth, O king, I shall (now) play with you.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एतच्छ्रुत्वा व्यवसितो निकृतिं समुपाश्रितः। जितमित्येव शकुनिर्युधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥९॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Having heard this and adopting unfair means, Shakuni, ever ready with the dice, sand to Yudhishthira, “Lo, I have won?"

verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              राजपुत्रा इमे राजन्शोभन्ते यैर्विभूषिताः। कुण्डलानि च निष्काश्च सर्वं राजविभूषणम्। एतन्मम धनं राजंस्तेन दीव्याम्यहं त्वया॥१०॥
verses.english: Yudhisthira said O_king, these princes here, who look resplendent in their ornaments and their earrings, and Nishkas and the royal ornaments on their persons are still my wealth. With this wealth, O king, I shall (now) play with you.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एतच्छ्रुत्वा व्यवसितो निकृतिं समुपाश्रितः। जितमित्येव शकुनिर्युधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥११॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Having heard this and adopting unfair means, Shakuni, ever ready with the dice, said to Yudhisthira, "Lo, I have won?”

verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              श्यामो युवा लोहिताक्षः सिंहस्कन्धो महाभुजः। नकुलो ग्लह एवैकी विद्ध्येतन्मम तद्धनम्॥१२॥
verses.english: Yudhisthira said This youthful, fair-coloured Nakula with mighty arms, with lion-like necks, and with red eyes is now one of my stakes.

verses.sanskrit: शकुनिरुवाच। प्रियस्ते नकुलो राजन्राजपुत्रो युधिष्ठिर। अस्माकं वशतां प्राप्तो भूयः केनेह दीव्यसे॥१३॥
verses.english: Shakuni said O king, O Yudhisthira, the prince Nakula is dear to you. (Know) he is already under our subjection (won by us). With what will you now play?

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एवमुक्त्वा तु तानक्षाञ्शकुनिः प्रत्यदीव्यत। जितमित्येव शकुनिर्युधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥१४॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Having said this, Shakuni cast the dice and thus spoke to Yudhisthira, Lo, I have won!"

verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              अयं धर्मान्सहदेवोऽनुशास्ति लोके ह्यस्मिन्पण्डिताख्यां गतश्च। अनर्हता राजपुत्रेण तेन दीव्याम्यहं चाप्रियवत्प्रियेण॥१५॥
verses.english: Yudhisthira said This Sahadeva administers justice, he has acquired a reputation for learning in this world. Though this prince does not deserve to be staked in play, yet with such dear object as my stake, I shall play, as if he is not so.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एतच्छ्रुत्वा व्यवसितो निकृतिं समुपाश्रितः। जितमित्येव शकुनिर्युधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥१६॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Having heard this and adopting unfair means, Shakuni, ever ready with the dice, said to Yudhisthira, "Lo I have won?"

verses.sanskrit: शकुनिरुवाच। माद्रीपुत्रौ प्रियौ राजंस्तवेमौ विजितौ मया। गरीयांसौ तु ते मन्ये भीमसेनधनञ्जयौ॥१७॥
verses.english: Shakuni said O king, the two sons of Madri are dear to you; but (know it for certain,) they have already) been won by me. It appears Bhimasena and Dhananjaya (Arjuna), are more loved by you (than these two).

verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              अधर्मं चरसे नूनं यो नावेक्षसि वै नयम्। यो नः सुमनसां मूढ विभेदं कर्तुमिच्छसि॥१८॥
verses.english: Yudhisthira said Fool, disregarding morality you sinfully act in thus trying to create disunion amongst us who are all of one heart.

verses.sanskrit: शकुनिरुवाच। गर्ते मत्तः प्रपतते प्रमत्तः स्थाणुमृच्छति। ज्येष्ठो राजन्वरिष्ठोऽसि नमस्ते भरतर्षभ॥१९॥
verses.english: Shakuni said O king, one who is intoxicated falls into a pit and remains there, being deprived of his power of motion. O best of the Bharata race, you are senior to us in age and in everything, I bow to you.

verses.sanskrit: स्वप्ने तानि न दृश्यन्ते जाग्रतो वा युधिष्ठिर। कितवा यानि दीव्यन्तः प्रलपन्त्युत्कटा इव॥२०॥
verses.english: O Yudhisthira, know, gamesters in the excitement of the play utter such raving as they would never do in their waking moments or in their dreams.
verses.bhavadeepa: मत्तः वित्तविवशचित्तत्वेनाधर्मकर्ता । स गर्त नरके स्थाणुं स्थाणुत्वम् ऋच्छति प्राप्नोति । आर्छतीति पाठे आङ् पूर्वस्य रूपम् । ज्येष्ठो वयसाधिकः । वरिष्ठो गुणैरधिकः ॥१९॥

verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              यो नः सङ्ख्ये नौरिव पारनेता जेता रिपूणां राजपुत्रस्तरस्वी। अनर्हता लोकवीरेण तेन दीव्याम्यहं शकुने फाल्गुनेन॥२१॥
verses.english: Yudhisthira said He who takes us like a boat to the other shore of the sea of battle, who is ever victorious over foes, who is endued with great activity and who is the only one hero in this world (in Arjuna). With that Falguni as stake, O Shakuni, though he does not deserve it, I shall (now) play.
verses.bhavadeepa: मत्तत्वमेवाह स्वप्न इति । मत्तस्य मम वचः क्षन्तव्यमिति भावः ॥२०॥

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एतच्छ्रुत्वा व्यवसितो निकृतिं समुपाश्रितः। जितमित्येव शकुनिर्युधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥२२॥
शकुनिरुवाच। अयं मया पाण्डवानां धनुर्धरः पराजितः पाण्डवः सव्यसाची। भीमेन राजन्दयितेन दीव्य यत्कैतवं पाण्डव तेऽवशिष्टम्॥२३॥
verses.english: Shakuni said This foremost of all wielders of bows, this Pandava Savyasachi (Arjuna) has been won by me. O king, O Pandava play now with (staking) your beloved Bhima, the only wealth that is now left to you.

verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              यो नो नेता यो युधि नः प्रणेता यथा वज्री दानवशत्रुरेकः। तिर्यक्प्रेक्षी सन्नतभ्रूर्महात्मा सिंहस्कन्धो यश्च सदाऽत्यमर्षी॥२४॥
verses.english: Yudhisthira said Though he does not deserve to be made a stake, I shall now play with staking Bhimasena, the prince who is our leader, who is foremost in fight like the wielder of thunder (Indra), the enerny of the Danavas, who is the illustrious hero with lion-like neck, arched eye-brows and expansive eyes, who is incapable of putting up with an insult, who is matchless in prowess in all the world, who is the foremost of all wielders of clubs and who grinds all foes.

verses.sanskrit: बलेन तुल्यो यस्य पुमान्न विद्यते गदाभृतामग्र्य इहारिमर्दनः। अनर्हता राजपुत्रेण तेन दीव्याम्यहं भीमसेनेन राजन्॥२५॥

वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एतच्छ्रुत्वा व्यवसितो निकृतिं समुपाश्रितः। जितमित्येव शकुनिर्युधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥२६॥
शकुनिरुवाच। बहुवित्तं पराजैषीर्भ्रातॄंश्च सहयद्विपान्। आचक्ष्व वित्तं कौन्तेय यदि तेऽस्त्यपराजितम्॥२७॥
verses.english: Shakuni said O son of Kunti, you have lost much wealth, heroes and elephants with your brothers. Tell us if you have anything else which you have not as yet lost.

verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              अहं विशिष्टः सर्वेषां भ्रातॄणां दयितस्तथा। कुर्यामहं जितः कर्म स्वयमात्मन्युपल्पुते॥२८॥
verses.english: Yudhisthira said I alone, the eldest of my brothers and beloved of all of them, am still not won (by you). If won by you, I shall do that which one who is won is bound to do.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एतच्छ्रुत्वा व्यवसितो निकृतिं समुपाश्रितः। जितमित्येव शकुनिर्युधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥२९॥
शकुनिरुवाच। एतत्पापिष्ठमकरोर्यदात्मानं पराजयेः। शिष्टे सति धने राजन्पाप आत्मपराजयः॥३०॥
verses.english: Shakuni said O king, you have allowed yourself to be won, an act which is worthy of a sinful man. When there is still wealth belonging to you, it is sinful to lose one's own self.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एवमुक्त्वा मताक्षस्तान्ग्लहे सर्वानवस्थितान्। पराजयल्लोकवीरानुक्त्वा राज्ञां पृथक्पृथक्॥३१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Having said this, (Shakuni), well-skilled in dice, spoke to all the brave kings present there of having won all the Pandavas one after the other.

verses.sanskrit: शकुनिरुवाच। अस्ति ते वै प्रिया राजन्ग्लह एकोऽपराजितः। पणस्व कृष्णां पाञ्चालीं तयात्मानं पुनर्जय॥३२॥
verses.english: Shakuni said O king, there is still one stake dear to you which is not yet won. Bet Krishna, (Draupadi), the princess of Panchala. By her, win yourself back.
verses.bhavadeepa: ग्लहे पणविषये राजानं प्रति एवमुक्त्वा राज्ञां पाण्डवानां पराजयं च लोकवीरान्प्रति उक्त्वा शकुनिरुवाचेत्युत्तरेण सम्बन्धः ॥३१॥

verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              नैव ह्रस्वा न महती न कृशा नातिरोहिणी। नीलकुञ्चितकेशी च तया दीव्याम्यहं त्वया॥३३॥
verses.english: Yudhisthira said I shall (now) play with you staking her who is neither short nor tall, neither lean nor corpulent, who possesses blue curly hair,
verses.bhavadeepa: आत्मानं प्रति पणं पुनर्जय दास्यान्मोचय । नो चेत् द्रौपदी वाऽस्मद्दासी भविष्यतीत्यर्थः॥३२॥

verses.sanskrit: शारदोत्पलपत्राक्ष्या शारदोत्पलगन्धया। शारदोत्पलसेविन्या रूपेण श्रीसमानया॥३४॥
verses.english: And eyes are like the leaves of the autumn lotus, and fragrance like that of the lily, who is like Sree herself in symmetry and grace,

verses.sanskrit: तथैव स्यादानुशंस्यात्तथा स्याद्रूपसम्पदा। तथा स्याच्छीलसम्पत्त्या यामिच्छेत्पुरुषः स्त्रियम्॥३५॥
verses.english: Who is such that for her softness of heart, wealth of beauty and virtue, one may desire her for a wife.
verses.bhavadeepa: शारदोत्पलसेविन्याः लक्ष्म्याः रूपेण समानया । श्रिया लावण्यसौभाग्यादिरूपया च समानया। श्रीति भिन्नं पदं छान्दसस्तृतीयाया लुक्पूर्वसवर्णो वा ॥३४॥

verses.sanskrit: सर्वैर्गुणैर्हि सम्पन्नामनुकूलां प्रियंवदाम्। यादृशीं धर्मकामार्थसिद्धिमिच्छेन्नरः स्त्रियम्॥३६॥
verses.english: Who possesses every accomplishment, who is compassionate and sweet speeched, who is such that for the acquisition of Dharma, Artha and Kama one may desire her for his wife.

verses.sanskrit: चरमं संविशति या प्रथमं प्रतिबुध्यते। आगोपालाविपालेभ्यः सर्वं वेद कृताकृतम्॥३७॥
verses.english: Who, retiring to bed last and rising from bed first, looks after the comforts of the cowherds and shepherds,
verses.bhavadeepa: धर्मकामार्थसिद्धिं धर्मकामयोरर्थयोः सिद्धिर्यया सा तथा ताम् । अर्थामिति पाठे सिद्धिमिव सिद्धिम् ॥३६॥

verses.sanskrit: आभाति पद्मवद्वक्त्रं सस्वेदं मल्लिकेव च। वेदीमध्या दीर्घकेशी ताम्रास्या नातिलोमशा॥३८॥
verses.english: Whose face when covered with sweat looks like the lotus or the wasp, who possesses flowing hair, red lips and body without down;

verses.sanskrit: तयैवंविधया राजन्पाञ्चाल्याहं सुमध्यमा। ग्लहं दीव्यामि चार्वङ्ग्या द्रौपद्या हन्त सौबल॥३९॥
verses.english: O king, O son of Subala, making that princess of Panchala, the slender-waisted Draupadi, as my stake, I shall (now) play with you.
verses.bhavadeepa: मल्लिकेव सुरभिरिति शेषः । सम्मोदो मल्लिकेव चेति गौडपाठे सम्मोदः परिमलः वेदीव कृशमध्या ॥३८॥

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एवमुक्ते तु वचने धर्मराजेन धीमता। धिग्धिगित्येव वृद्धानां सभ्यानां निःसृता गिरः॥४०॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said When this was said by the wise Dharmaraja (Yudhisthira), “Fie! Fie!" were the words uttered by all the elders that were present in the assembly.

verses.sanskrit: चुक्षुभे सा सभा राजन्राज्ञां सञ्जज्ञिरे शुचः। भीष्मद्रोणकृपादीनां स्वेदश्च समजायत॥४१॥
verses.english: O king, the whole assembly was agitated. The kings began to grieve. Bhisma, Drona and Kripa were covered with perspiration.

verses.sanskrit: शिरो गृहीत्वा विदुरो गतसत्व इवाभवत्। आस्ते ध्यायन्नधोवक्त्रो निःश्वसन्निव पन्नगः॥४२॥
verses.english: Vidura, holding his head between his hands, sat like one who has lost his reason. He sat with down cast face giving away to his own thoughts and sighing like a snake.

verses.sanskrit: धृतराष्ट्रस्तु तं हृष्टः पर्यपृच्छत्पुनः पुनः। किं जितं किं जितमिति ह्याकारं नाभ्यरक्षत॥४३॥
verses.english: (But) Dhritarashtra, being glad at heart, could not conceal his emotions and asked again and again, "is the stake won?” “Is the stake won???

verses.sanskrit: जहर्ष कर्णोऽतिभृशं सह दुःशासनादिभिः। इतरेषां तु सभ्यानां नेत्रेभ्यः प्रापतज्जलम्॥४४॥
verses.english: Karna with Dushasana and others laughed aloud, but tears began to flow from the eyes of all those that were present in the assembly.

verses.sanskrit: सौबलस्त्वभिघायैव जितकाशी मदोत्कटः। जितमित्येव तानक्षान्पुररेवान्वपद्यत॥४५॥
verses.english: The son of Subala (Shakuni), proud of success, and flurried with excitement, repeating “You have still one stake dear to you” said, "Lo, I have won!” He then took up the dice that had been cast.
